This is a thick plastic spork that is just somewhat stronger than a typical plastic utensil. It is BPA-free and is food and dishwasher safe. There is a fork on one end with one of the tines that has a "knife-like" edge. There is a spoon on the other end. The center holes can be used to fasten this to a backpack using the reusable teather it comes packaged with.

I got this because many times when I go on a staycation, I pack a cooler with yogurt and stuff for day travel. This is perfect for that. I ate with the spoon and fork fine but I could not cut anything of substance with the knife. I think $4.99 is reasonable for what this is but the knife-like edge is completely useless. A butter knife cuts better. However, the spoon and fork are good for any "away-type" eating such as camping, backpacking, or just a staycation with a cooler in tow.

Even though the price is right, the reason I give this 3 stars is because the knife is useless and the thick plastic has a different mouth feel and pick-up ability. For instance, when I was eating yogurt with the spoon, I could not scrape the container as easily with the spoon end as I could with the [[ASIN:B07M8K5VQ8 Titanium Spork]]. This is good enough but neither their Titanium spork or this one is great.

I attached two pictures. The first photo is of this set and the second photo is with my Titanium version on the right end for comparison purposes.

text_fidelity_a:
SE Survivor Series Portable Chain Saw with Ergonomic Handles - CS001 I like to do a lot of outside work. That includes cutting down dead wood and keeping a rather large yard in order. I don't tend to use a lot of power tools as the guys all have their own which they take with them. That has left me with little to work with. I got this little hand portable chain saw not only for survival, but to use around my property when I need to cut some significant wood. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a rather hard to get into package. Once I was able to cut into it, I found that it has two handles with cord on them, a chain for sawing and a nylon carrying case with a belt loop on it to keep it handy.

HOW DOES THIS GO TOGETHER?
The handles slip through the rings on either end of this saw. It is important that you lay the chain out before installing the handles so that you have the handles in the right direction so that you can pull on them and the saw blades will be going into the wood.

Once you have them in the right direction (and both facing the same way) then you slip the loop into the ring and over the handle and it stays put.

HOW DO YOU USE IT?
You put the blades into the branch you want to cut, cross the handles in front of the branch and pull from side to side to keep the chain moving back and forth.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is a GREAT SAW! I don't have tons of body strength, but this saw has regularly cut through 3 and 4 inch wood for me. I LOVE how fast it is. It only takes me a few minutes most of the time unless it is a very hard piece of wood.

CAN YOU CUT ALREADY CUT WOOD?
This does not work that well if the branch is already cut unless you can brace it into place and have a good resistance to keep it stable while you saw it. I find it is best when used on a branch still attached to a tree most of the time, or a really large part of a tree that might be dead, but it stays put.

OILING
I use a lubricant from our freeze dryer which is made for vacuum motors. It works really great and the one I use is food safe so it won't hurt the environment like fuel will. Small amount, not really worth discussing for most people, but it sure beats smelling like petroleum oil in the case.

CASE
The case is big enough for the saw to fit into, but I tend to keep a plastic bag in there to put the chain into to keep it from leaking through the case over time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a fabulous little saw. I love having it around. I have used it a lot and really am thankful to have it. Camping, hiking, or just working around the yard when the power tools are missing make this one of my favorite new tools I own.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. SO HAPPY to have this. If it is kept lubricated and not left out in the weather, this should last a while, perhaps only the handle cords might need replacing over time.
text_fidelity_b: SE Survivor Series Portable Chain Saw with Ergonomic Handles - CS001

Heated Gloves for Women Touchscreen Rechargeable Battery Electric Hand Warmers Winter Gloves Ski Gloves for Outdoor Sports Cycling Riding Skiing Skating I’ve never owned heated gloves before, but these are amazing! The design allows you to easily tighten several areas of the glove for a better fit, and you can still use your smart phone with the fingertips, which is great. The batteries have light indicators to show you roughly how charged they are, and they are easy to put in to the glove and remove, as well as to charge. Turning the gloves on and off it’s also as simple as the press of a button on top, which is easy to operate even while wearing the gloves.

As for the heat distribution, it’s not as even as I would like: it is most concentrated at the thumb and doesn’t distribute as much to the other areas. Even so, it’s incredibly soothing and pleasant, and on the most frigid days, boy does it make a difference! There are three levels of intensity for the heat, so you can decide what feels best. For me, I either like 45% or 70%. The hottest setting (100%), because it’s so concentrated in the thumb, feels a little uncomfortable for me personally. These were so straightforward on how to use them, I didn’t need the instruction manual, but I read it anyway just to see if I was missing anything. I learned there is a spare cable in case the one inside the glove wears out for whatever reason, which is nice.

Overall, these are excellent for cold weather and people whose hands get particularly cold. Even off-season, if you have arthritis or any hand pain, these are terrific for that as well. Terrific invention!
text_fidelity_b: Heated Gloves for Women Touchscreen Rechargeable Battery Electric Hand Warmers Winter Gloves Ski Gloves for Outdoor Sports Cycling Riding Skiing Skating

My husband and I both enjoy a casual game of tennis.

With this tool I am able to toss my kids the ball - I hold onto the elastic cord a few feet away from the ball with my other hand and then it’s very easy for me to get the ball after they hit it back or miss the ball.
My process so far has been first starting out, directly to their racket - here they work on holding the racket and then swinging the racket when the ball comes.
Next we work on finding the ball with their racket where I can toss the ball just out of the way of the racket and they have to adjust where their racket is to hit the ball.

Kharma Khare Reincarnated Lite Non Slip Eco-Friendly Yoga Mat - 4 Mm (Black) NOTE: I received a free sample of this yoga mat to review.

I have multiple yoga mats; I tend to select different ones for different uses. The one I rely on the most is my [[ASIN:B00AB3LLVS Manduka eKO Lite Yoga Mat]], as it is lightweight, thin (which I prefer), and the most dependably non-slip mat I have ever tried.

This Kharma Khare mat is slightly thicker than my Manduka eKo Lite. However, unlike some thick yoga mats, it is not a squishy thickness, which I can't stand--rather, it is nice and firm, and it feels great under your feet. Standing on the mat, I got great grip and felt that the mat was very secure. When my hands were on the mat--in downward dog, for example--I thought that the grip was decent, but not QUITE as good as with my eKo mat. Still, overall I feel confident practicing yoga on this mat.

To me, the main selling point of the Kharma Khare mat is that it is made from recycled tires--love this! Mine did have a bit of a rubbery odor when I first unrolled it, but this dissipated after I 1) wiped it down with the included yoga mat wipes (not sure if this is standard, but I received 20 2-packs of these), and 2) left it unrolled for several days. The only other (minor) negative of this mat is that the black color easily shows dusty footprints; I noticed this more using this mat than with any of my other mats. Still, I would highly recommend this mat, especially for the eco-conscious yogi, and my final rating is 4 1/2 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Kharma Khare Reincarnated Lite Non Slip Eco-Friendly Yoga Mat - 4 Mm (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
K-MingleSo Upgraded Portable Folding Stool, 13 Inch Camping Stool for Adults Fishing Hiking Gardening and Beach with Carry Bag, Hold Up to 450lbs[Camo] I am recovering from a walking issue. As I continue to recover, I am trying to find ways to include some easy to store stools or small places to sit if I find myself in a situation where I have to stand for too long. This looked perfect.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes all disassembled in a drawstring bag with basic instruction sheet.

HOW TO ASSEMBLE
You take the elastic loop off of the pieces. Then you quickly assemble the pieces which are shock corded together to make a nice stool.

PHONE POUCH
There is a pocket on the front that fits most phones.

WHAT'S THE PROBLEM?
I was so thrilled to get this, but when I put it together, I was not sure if I should laugh or cry. The stool is TINY. I am talking TODDLER TINY. It is not quite 12 inches off the ground and there is nothing to hold on to to get up. This is almost like sitting on the floor- not quite.

If I were to open this up and sit in public while waiting, I am sure I would like weird. It is a very tiny stool which is perfect if you are a toddler. As an adult, it is ridiculous looking.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I had high hopes for this thing. It is so ridiculously tiny that I can not use it. Maybe the cat can have it be her seat in the summer when we are camping. Maybe there is a toad that needs a chair.

MY RATING
ONE STAR. This should be pointed out to be for children or very very small people. It is not suitable for most adults I know- even older kids laughed when I showed it to them. For toddlers, I would give this four stars (because it is tough to put together for toddler ages). For adults ONE STAR.
text_fidelity_b: K-MingleSo Upgraded Portable Folding Stool, 13 Inch Camping Stool for Adults Fishing Hiking Gardening and Beach with Carry Bag, Hold Up to 450lbs[Camo]

SecurityIng® 3 Modes Waterproof 4200LM 7X XM-L2 Temperature Control Special Design LED Bicycle Light Super Bright Bicycle Headlight LED Charging Lamp LED Bike Light with 8.4V 7800mAh Rechargeable Battery & Charger This is a bike light that wants to be a lighthouse beacon. Seriously – you could guide ships through a dense fog with this light. It’s bright with a capital B!

That’s not a bad thing. On a dark rural road or trail when there are no streetlights, this lamp will literally turn night into day. However, it can be a problem in more populated areas or when there are oncoming cars. If this is not positioned properly with the light beam facing down, you will completely blind anyone coming in the opposite direction. This is a light you need to use with caution when around others.

The build quality throughout is excellent. The light body is all metal and very sturdy. There are a lot of cooling fins in the body to help dissipate heat. Still, even with the fins, this gets very hot after it’s been on for a while.

The light attaches to the handle bars via rubber rings that slip over two mounting brackets. If properly positioned they hold the lamp tight, but you do need to fiddle with the rubber rings a bit to ensure a tight fit. While a permanent mounting option would be nice, I can see the advantage of the rubber rings since it makes putting the lamp on or taking it off a tool-less process.

The battery pack connects to the lamp with a stout cord that also has a screw on jacket to keep everything attached while riding. The battery pack itself has a rubberized coating plus a rubber jacket to keep it weather tight. It stows in a thick nylon pouch with sturdy Velcro closures and straps to keep it closed up and attached to the bike. Given all that protection, I have zero concerns about water splashing on the battery causing any problems.

The cord between the battery and the battery pack is a little over 30 inches long which proved to be ample for me to put the lamp on the handle bars and the power pack on the front fork.

It’s very simple to use – only one button which is located on the back of the lamp. Press it once, and it turns on the full set of 7 lamps. Press it again and only the middle three lamps are lit (which is still very bright). Press it a third time and it starts to strobe on/off (all 7 bulbs). One more press and it turns off.

It is VERY annoying that you can’t go from ON to OFF without going through the strobe mode.

It includes a wall charger to recharge the battery pack. The stated battery life is 4 hours at full power which proved to be pretty accurate. The battery is rated as 7800mAh, which is impressive. What is not impressive is the battery life indicator – it’s located on the charger, rather than the device. So, to determine how much battery life is left you have to disconnect the lamp, connect the battery to the charger, and look at the LED on the charger. Plus, it only has two colors – green means 30% to 100% capacity left; red means less than 30%. Not exactly helpful in use.

Another miss is the manual – it literally is missing. No documentation at all came in the box. Granted, this is a pretty easy device to figure out, but at this price point a manual or instruction sheet of some type really should be included.

Although the negatives concerning the user interface and manual temp me to drop this to 4 stars, I’ll keep the rating at 5 stars for two main reasons: build quality and performance. This truly is the most powerful light I’ve ever used, equaling the performance of a car’s headlamp. Provided that this is used properly to avoid blinding oncoming traffic/bicyclists, it is a huge benefit at night especially on a trail. Due to the power of it, however, I would NOT recommend it for urban/suburban street use since the risk of harm to others is just too high.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: SecurityIng® 3 Modes Waterproof 4200LM 7X XM-L2 Temperature Control Special Design LED Bicycle Light Super Bright Bicycle Headlight LED Charging Lamp LED Bike Light with 8.4V 7800mAh Rechargeable Battery & Charger

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives SAT002-BX Flashback Tini Knife, Black SOG has been in the industry a long time. They offer an affordable value in the knife world. They constantly try to innovate and carry Lifetime Warranties on their products. Some of their designs are fantastic. Some are duds. The Flashback is an awesome every day carry folder that is nearly perfect but just misses shy. I still managed to pick up this straight clip model as well as a tanto version.

Packaging: This is the black box version. Not the retail box version. It doesn't matter, you get the same knife in both boxes but one doesn't have a clear window to view the blade and the other is just a black manufacturer's box that says SOG. It's not about the box, it's about what's inside.

First glance: This thing screams cool. I just love the color scheme, look of the blade, the total design reminds me of a slick silver on black race car set up. The clip is reversible, but already comes in my preferred carry designation. It rides deep in the pocket and retains firmly to the pocket. I haven't had one instance of it coming loose or getting hung up on seatbelts or the like in my daily use.

Picking it up: I believe SOG advertises these Flashback knives around 3.8 oz. It feels heavier, but I don't have a scale to confirm. Either way, it's fairly light. Disable the safety, and then never use it again. I'm actually of the mindset SOG should just delete their safeties on most of their assisted folders, but your mileage may vary. If it gives you a warm fuzzy to use it, then do so. I think it just takes away from the attractiveness of the design and is unnecessary. First use flicking it open and you realize SOG really meant this thing was fast. It opens authoritatively, too, so hold on to it. Snaps into a firm lock position and is ready to use. The blade is AUS-8 steel and comes hair shaving sharp out of the box. AUS-8 is OK, but I wish SOG would use some better steels in their builds. It'll be fine for the use of everyday carry, however. I'm not a huge Tanto fan, but I had to have that model in addition to this straight clip Flashback I picked up due to how much I liked the straight clip after carrying a few days. The Tanto was supposed to be a gift, but I think I'm keeping it, too. As for the grip, you can get a firm purchase on the blade as a result of the aggressive gimping. I think SOG nailed this one unlike some of their other designs. It fits my hand so well and provides a level of confidence in use as result.

Build Quality: Now here's where things get tricky. SOG is a mass market knife maker. Meaning they pump them out, check on the quality so often, and use cheap labor to build it. One example can be outstanding in build and the next will be ok for the value. The tanto I received has perfect blade centering. The straight clip model is off to one side. Both are well built, but inherent in a lot of SOG designs there is some side-to-side play in each once the blade is in the locked position. It has something to do with their locking design as it was also inherent in the Aegis I've previously owned. This is where I knock these knives down a star as others in the same price category like Cold Steel and Spyderco don't have these issues.

Overall: I love carrying this knife. I do prefer the straight clip blade design and would recommend that to purchasers as the blade shape is more useful, at least to me. I still had to have this tanto version in addition. There are some caveats that come in the mass-produced build quality, but if you want a well-built everyday folder that has a solid value than you shouldn't be disappointed in the Flashbacks from SOG. I would suggest shopping around a bit and making sure you do get the best price, however, as these can fluctuate. With a few shortcomings, this still comes as a recommended buy.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives SAT002-BX Flashback Tini Knife, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Abus Bordo 5700 Folding Lock The most popular good quality bicycle locks around where I live are hardened steel U-locks and hardened steel chains. Bicyclists like them because newer bike racks are designed for those types of locks and people know how to use them. This folding lock is about 2 pounds (with the included plastic holder, a little less without), which compares to about 2.5 pounds for a chain lock or U-lock with similar security. It also folds up more compactly than a chain or U-lock so is easier to carry both on your bike or in a bag. In use, the folding design works well for most bike racks, though it can be awkward for bike racks with tight clearance.

Abus rates this a 7 out of 15 on their security scale, so it can be cut with large bolt cutters (but so can medium-quality chain locks or U-locks). Some people complain that a thief with the right tools can break the rivets on this lock pretty easily, but realistically thieves in most cities are more likely to use giant bolt cutters, which can cut the metal bars on this lock even more easily than the rivets.

If you're locking your bike in a high-theft area, you really need to use a better quality lock than this or even 2 locks. This lighter weight lock might be good for a secondary lock (locking your front wheel and frame to the bike rack) while you use a better lock to lock your rear wheel and frame to the bike rack.

My main complaint is that this lock costs twice as much as a medium-quality chain lock or U-lock, so I can only give this 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Abus Bordo 5700 Folding Lock

text_fidelity_a:
Bilbear Adjustable Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat,Portable Nordic Strap for Hamstring Curls,Hamstring Stretch,Crunch,Sit-ups,Nordic Curl Machine at Home,Withstand 400lbs I've been looking at Nordic Hamstring Curl straps, checking out review and pics and videos. It seems that most of the ones available on Amazon are pretty much the same, and many have the same complaints, so when I saw this one - the Bilbear Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat - available on Vine, I ordered it.

First off, it has no chemical or rubber smells or strong smells of any kind. In addition to the strap itself, it comes with a small rubber mat for your knees, like a thinner miniature yoga mat - and a bag to put everything in.

Overall this item looked like the pics on the listing, and worked as expected. The strap is really really long, but you can use the buckle to shorten it. We found it easier to use as a foot holddown than for Nordic hamstring curls, but successfully did both repeatedly. The mat is a little thinner that my yoga mat, and it's not that large, so you need to keep your knees in the same spot on the floor if you use it. The foam is pretty comfortable, the door anchor is huge - I can't imagine a door is could slip under.

One of the complaints I read on other Nordic Hamstring Curl mats was true of this one, also - the buckle slips as you work out, so the strap gets a very tiny bit longer with each rep, but if you do a number of reps, that slippage becomes noticeable. Our other issue is how narrow the foot holders are from one side of one to the other side of the other. My husband has size 12 feet, and in his shoes, he had to keep his feet crammed together. I have much smaller but wider feet, and I found I wanted more space so my feet could be a little further apart.

Is the Bilbear Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat for you? Well, if you prefer keeping your feet together when doing sit-ups, crunches, Nordic hamstring curls and other exercises you use a foot holddown for, you may find this very useful. Yes, the strap slips, but as far as I can tell, this is common to all similar products. I might have given this 3 stars, but because price, features and issues seem to similar to competitors, I'm giving it 4 stars based on comparable items. Happy training!
text_fidelity_b: Bilbear Adjustable Nordic Hamstring Curl Strap with Kneeling Mat,Portable Nordic Strap for Hamstring Curls,Hamstring Stretch,Crunch,Sit-ups,Nordic Curl Machine at Home,Withstand 400lbs

text_fidelity_a:
American Athletic Shoe Women's Tricot Lined Ice Skates These skates are great for the price! I wear a size 9-9.5 shoe and ordered a size 9. These skates fit fine with tights, didn't try with stockings. I'm a beginner ice skater and these were excellent for me. They are fairly stiff in the ankle - but in a good way - you don't want to roll your ankle. One of the biggest problems that I remember with having rental skates in the past is that my feet turned inward, in these skates my feet were straight and in the right position (i.e., skating directly on the blade, instead of the side). Can't say whether that was due to the skates or my technique, but these were FAR better than any rental skates I've used. They're pretty comfy, I may add an insole for extra comfort. All in all these are excellent skates.
I took them to a skate shop and had them sharpened before I skated with them (about thirty bucks, but it was a pro shop and it seemed like they did a good job and it was worth the money!). Not sure if that was necessary, but a friend who is a serious skater said that you should always get your skates sharpened if they're brand new. (The guy at the skate shop said so, too.)
Remember to buy skate guards and to completely dry off your blades!
text_fidelity_b: American Athletic Shoe Women's Tricot Lined Ice Skates

Fitness First High Intensity Vibrating Foam Roller If you have back pain like I do, you'll appreciate a good massage. This tubular looking thing is made of a very dense foam... so dense that when I first saw it, I thought it was hard plastic... but notit's not, there is some give to it. It turns out, when you place td his behind you in a chair, it's that density that keeps it holding its shape while it does its job. While I've been using it in an easy chair, I would say it could take a person's full weight without a problem.

It's got 3 speeds, but I find the lowest of the 3 is plenty strong enough to give me a good massage. If you needed something stronger, it's there.

At just under 6 inches in diameter and 13 inches long, it's a good size to slide behind yourself in an easy chair. There's a handle on one end that snaps out to reveal the recharging port, and on the other hand is the 3 position knob to control the speed. Of course, it comes with a charger.

The only downside is that with its dense foam and strong massage, it seems a little jarring if you try using it on your neck. Some kind of cushion would definitely be in order for that.

bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
1071 cubic inches
17” x 10.5” x 6”
6 1/2” mesh pockets
Covers about 5 1/2” of bottles
Straps 3” wide
Hard to adjust shoulder straps, especially to loosen them
Straps feel soft and pliable
This pack has 3 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a small zippered pocket. In the front is a mesh compartment which is held closed by a strap and buckle. I did not like having a mesh compartment.
Pros:
- Lightweight
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying it
- Side pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Medium sized zippered pouch inside the large compartment – this is where the pack is stored when folded
- Large pocket inside on the back of the large compartment
- 1 extra loop on outside bottom of pack.
- Extra side support straps
Cons:
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.
- Some padding on the back panel
- Shoulder straps were several layers of mesh but NOT fortified with the nylon fabric
- Things stored in front mesh compartment would get dirtier and wetter than in a pack with a zippered fabric covered compartment.

I returned this pack. It was a nice foldable pack, but I didn't like the mesh pocket in the front.

text_fidelity_a:
19Pcs Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands - 4 Pull Up Bands, 3 Exercise Resistance Loop Bands, 2 Core Sliders, Jump Rope, Handles, Door Anchor, Wrist Wraps for Body Stretching/Power Training I am a senior, and was exercising religiously at a fitness center, prior to the virus. I won't be going back.
We live in a senior condo, and I have no space for fitness hardware.

After almost three months of not exercising, I was getting depressed, and purchased an inexpensive set of bands from Amazon. My only prior expensive with bands was a short rehab stint for a frozen shoulder and stiff neck.

Being new to bands, I didn't know what to get,.
The inexpensive bands I bought, didn't do much for me.

I found there are three primary types of resistance bands.
The open ended rubber hose style, that can have handles attached,
The closed loop design. This product being reviewed is closed loop.
The very wide open ended bands I used in rehab. Those are very flexible and can be used open, or knotted. They don't seem to be widely available.

After buying the open ended rubber hose style, I started exercising in front of You Tube Fitness videos. In my case, senior fitness videos. Although I'm a male, I use the Senior Fitness with Meredith, exercise. No products are advertised for sale on the site. I quickly saw the advantage in having different sets of bands. There is also an advantage in having different lengths. Different exercises utilize the open ended rubber hose style, while others lend themselves to the closed loop. The thicker closed loop bands seem safer for lower body exercises. I first used the thinner rubber type bands for lower body exercises. One slipped off my foot, and boomeranged back into my throat. Ouch.

Having different sets keeps you from wasting time by having to stop and change your bands, such as removing handles and tying loops during exercises, and then untying them. Just switch to the right band.

This product being reviewed has closed loops, of varied resistance. Depending on your level of fitness, they can wear you out as you change to thicker bands. A few items in this set were an overkill for me. I won't use the jump rope or the sliders. The sliders are useful though for moving furniture. They are the same size as the large sliders I keep under my sofa, for ease of moving. The quality of the bands that come with this product seem excellent.

The items in this product can easily be returned to the original bag, taking up almost no space. Don't rip the box as it also comes in handy for storage.

Finally, if you are new to bands, I suggest watching some videos utilizing different bands, and starting with the type that appeals to you.
text_fidelity_b: 19Pcs Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands - 4 Pull Up Bands, 3 Exercise Resistance Loop Bands, 2 Core Sliders, Jump Rope, Handles, Door Anchor, Wrist Wraps for Body Stretching/Power Training

SupeRun Under Desk Treadmill, 2 in 1 Walking Pad Treadmill Quiet for Office Home Use, Portable Desk Treadmill with Remote Control, LED Display for Walking and Jogging Bottom line: If you don’t have the space for a full-sized treadmill, don’t expect to use it for running, and want to keep the cost as low as possible, this may fit the bill. It’s super compact but there are some significant limitations including the lack of a key safety feature: a foot-operated shut off switch.

Full review: This comes fully assembled, and is very well packaged with ample padding and straps to protect it. It even has thin wood plates at both ends to guard against damage. An A-plus for packaging and in-transit protection.

Compared with a full-size treadmill, this is a snap to move around. With all the packing material the box is around 50 pounds. Not toss-around light, but not so heavy that it’s a chore to move. I was able to get it down a full set of stairs by myself, and I’m no spring chicken! Once unpacked, it can be tilted and moved around on two small wheels at the front.

All operations are done via the included remote. It has some very nice features including a count-down mode (you set the time, distance or calories and it counts down and stops when complete). It also has an auto slow-down mode when you turn it off. For example, if you’re using it at 1.5 mph and turn it off, the speed slowly ramps down to zero to avoid a lurching stop. It also has a three count start-up: when you turn it on, it counts to three (and beeps) before starting to make sure you have the time to set yourself properly. The display is very large and easy to see at a distance.

Unfortunately, there are also some disappointments with this. The build quality is lightweight, but generally adequate for the price point except for the most important area: belt tension/operation smoothness. The belt has a waviness to it and is not held taut side-to-side. It causes noise from rubbing, and also makes the belt not nearly as comfortable as a real treadmill belt. It can be adjusted (an Allen wrench is provided for turning the adjustment screws) but even after fiddling with it for some time it still was not great.

The unit is fine for walking but I would really hesitate about using this for running. The deck is not strong enough to handle pounding from running, nor is the unit stable enough to allow such activity safely, in my opinion. The unit comes with a default max speed of 3.5mph, but you can override that to 5mph.

The motor is rated at 2.5hp but I think that’s overstated based on how much the speed lags when under load.

The speed can only be adjusted in increments of 0.5 mph. That’s a significant limitation when this is used for walking since you can’t fine-tune the speed to what feels best (unless what feels best is exactly at the 0.5 mph increment).

The maintenance instructions state to lube the belt monthly. Oil is provided. However, getting the oil under the belt is difficult. The instructions are sparse – you’re supposed to lift an edge of the belt and lube the underside, but actually doing that is very cumbersome, difficult and messy.

The included operating manual is very basic and not all that informative. It is a thick booklet but that’s due to it having info in several languages. It lacks detail and is not well-written.

The above issues could be lived with, especially considering the price. However, there are two issues that are far more serious: not having the unit respond to the remote all the time; and the lack of a foot-operated off switch.

The unit does not always respond properly to the remote. I can press the speed to increase and nothing happens. I press it again and it jumps up 2 speeds. Considering that the only way to operate the unit is with the remote, having it fail to recognize commands is a serious downside. Thinking it was due to weak batteries I swapped out the provided batteries for two known good ones. No change in how the remote worked (or failed to work).

Lastly, and most important, the unit lacks what I consider to be a critical safety item: a foot operated switch. If you’re on the treadmill and the remote fails to work (or you drop the remote) there’s no way to turn the treadmill off. Having to hop off the machine while it is running is a huge safety risk.

Overall, my rating is 2.5 stars. Granted, it is hugely inexpensive compared with a full-size treadmill, but even for the price the limitations are significant and have an impact on how this can be used. If it had a foot-mounted off switch I’d rate it at 3.5 stars, but the lack of such an important safety feature – regardless of how inexpensive this is – keeps my score in the below average territory.
text_fidelity_b: SupeRun Under Desk Treadmill, 2 in 1 Walking Pad Treadmill Quiet for Office Home Use, Portable Desk Treadmill with Remote Control, LED Display for Walking and Jogging

RELIFE Exercise Bike with Adjusable Resistance & Comfortable Seat Indoor Stationary Cycling Bike with LCD Monitor Fitness Bicycle with Heavy Duty Flywheel for Home Gym Cardio Workout Machine New Version, Weight Capacity 400LBS This is a nice basic stationary bike. Assembly was straightforward and without any issues. In use, it seems well made and sturdy. It's a typical flywheel design with a knob to adjust a resistance onto the wheel itself. The seat is completely adjustable for height and can be position more forward or rearward to further adjust your position relative to the pedals and the handlebars. The seat itself is nicely padded and reasonably comfortable, although I am considering replacing the seat with something wider. It uses a standard bicycle seat, so that should be an easy thing to do.

The pedals are those "steel trap" type with the jagged contacts that require you to wear shoes. I'm okay with that, but theres a nylon strap system that surrounds your toes. My size 12 feet means I'm pedaling on my toes. The pedals, therefore, were the first thing to be replaced. Again, it uses standard picycly parts so replacement was easy.

The control module is a simple battery operated counter. It can track miles, calories or time... or it can be set to cycle through the various measurements as you go. Theres no connection to the adjustable wheel resistance, so things like calorie burn are obviously just an approximation, at best. But that's pretty typical, I'm sure.

Overall, I recommend this bike. It seems well made and it gets the job done.
text_fidelity_b: RELIFE Exercise Bike with Adjusable Resistance & Comfortable Seat Indoor Stationary Cycling Bike with LCD Monitor Fitness Bicycle with Heavy Duty Flywheel for Home Gym Cardio Workout Machine New Version, Weight Capacity 400LBS

text_fidelity_a:
The Firm TransFIRMer The FIRM Supercharged Sculpting workout is a highly stylized workout with electronica, artistically designed sets and a clean, sleek mood. This is a combination of traditional weight training with aerobics using the necessary TransFIRMer. Most of the exercises are recognizable as traditional exercises like plank or sit-ups and squats.

The lunges seem easier to do with the TransFIRMer, although weights are used throughout most of the exercises to give them a little more edge. The workout is followed by a brief stretching segment, but if you want to totally relax, there is a "Bonus: 8-minute Stretch Workout."

This set also includes two additional DVDs: The FIRM Ultimate Calorie Blaster and The FIRM Aerobic Body Shaping. If you have any issues with your knees, you may need to try various workouts to see which ones you can manage. I found the Ultimate Calorie Blaster DVD was hard on the knees.

"The TransFIRMer was designed with multiple uses in mind and has 5 different configurations to take each workout to the next level." ~ pg. 6

The TransFIRMer can be positioned in five different ways to increase the possibilities:

6" TransFIRMer - The green section can be used alone
8" TransFIRMer - The blue section can be used alone
14" TransFIRMer - The blue and green sections used together
Side-by-Side TransFIRMer - The blue and green sections placed next to each other
Incline TransFIRMer - The green piece fits into the blue piece for a convenient and stable incline.

"You can adjust the intensity of the workout depending on how high you step." ~ pg. 7

The workout booklet has some interesting rotation calendars so you can plan out 21 days. There is also a section on healthy eating tips, an eating plan, 21-day diet plan, list of 100-calorie snacks and list of 200-calorie snacks. A substitution list makes the diet easier to follow especially if you are eating out and want to still keep to the diet plan.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Special Edition Smart Watch, Charcoal Woven, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Battery
I’ve had this watch for about a year and the battery life has gone from a week to about 24 hours. The advertised quick text replies didn’t work on any platform for months after the watch came out, and after having the watch for a year they eventually reported that they would never work with the iPhone (this was not reported prior to the release).

Period tracking
The menstrual cycle tracking is not remotely accurate. For the first few months after it came out it seemed like it was just predicting The same date(s) each month (which was not that far off and not all that unhelpful) but at some point it got off and trying to change it didn’t work and it’s never been even close again.

Data entry
After the most recent software update it was supposed to be possible to (finally) enter exercise and water directly on the watch but it does not work. It’s possible to enter the information and looks like it is saving, but it does not actually transfer to the dashboard, and when I check back on the watch later the data is gone.

Sleep
The sleep tracking accuracy is harder to determine. It does not seem to match with how I feel, but the hours in bed are correct about half the time. This is not so bad actually because I get up multiple times during the night and am extremely restless, which I would expect to throw off any wearable sleep tracker. A battery life that allows for sleep tracking was one reason I was interested in getting this in the first place, but it is not accurate enough to be helpful.

Heart rate
The heart rate tracking is actually pretty accurate as long as I wear the watch tight enough over the pulse point on my wrist. It also creates a graph of heart rate trends that are accurate. This has been the most accurate and helpful feature of the watch.

Dashboard
The dashboard is not at all user friendly. It is hard to enter information, and I have to use the website to enter my workouts since the automatic tracking, app entering, and watch entering do not work. Entering calories is so glitchy and time consuming it is not worth doing. After the last update I have to log into the dashboard every single time whether or not I select the option to keep me logged in.

Step counting
I can’t say exactly how accurate the step counting is, but it seems like it is pretty close. Days I walk more it’s higher, and the times I have walked on a treadmill and can watch the steps go up as I walk it seems to match closely.

Apps
This is one of the worst and most disappointing parts of this “smart watch.” NONE of the apps work, and they often cause my phone to freeze. Apps that I installed before realizing that they would not work will randomly appear back on the watch sometimes for no reason. Storing music on the watch is a complicated process that is not worth it, and playing music with it requires a subscription to Deezer which does not work as well as Apple Music and when I had it crashed all the time.

No other device I have ever crashes or causes any problems. After my experience with this watch and the lower price point on the new apple watches I am never purchasing another Fitbit product and strongly suggest avoiding them.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Special Edition Smart Watch, Charcoal Woven, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

Royal Medical Direct 180-Piece First Aid Kit - Hospital-Grade Emergency Medical Supplies for Traveling, Hiking, Camping, Home, or Auto - Portable, Lightweight and Travel Ready needed a first aid kit for a week long trip I was about to take with several family friends and parents to Big Bend National Park, I have been countless times growing up. This trip would be my 6 year old daughter's first trip so I wanted to ensure I had THE first aid kit.
After researching several versions, I decided this would be the one. I came to this decision after reading the reviews made by EMTs or others who have real experience in first aid. They all basically said the same thing... great kit, but I added...and that was the point. There isn't one perfect first aid kit that has everything unless you want something grossly overweight and take up way too much room in your pack.
There are two items that are really lacking from this first aid kit 1. blood clotting agent & 2. aspirin. That's what I added to it after buying it.
I don't like that the bag is not water proof. One reviewer stated that their pack got wet and the kit got soaked which ruined all the band aids, bandages, guaze, etc. I bought a water proof sack and I keep it in there at all times now, problem solved.
I carried this kit during my short hike to The Window and on my long overnight hike to the South Rim. I didn't need it, but knew that if I did it was in arm's reach. Good purchase. Going to purchase another one for my wife's car.

BLACKHAWK 40TP03CT AMBI TecGrip Pocket Holster, Size 03, Coyote Tan I wanted to like this, I really did! It fit my Sig Sauer P365 but very loosely. That was the first problem I encountered. The grip of the outer material is not in question. It's good. In the waistband either up against skin or underwear the holster stayed in place and allowed for an easy draw. Too easy. The holster also allowed for an easy drop to the floor because it in no way holds tightly to your firearm. I bent over to pick something up and my gun hit the floor! I can't imagine what would have happened had I been out at the store. No matter how I jammed the gun in it just didn't stay securely inside the holster.
But my biggest problem. Which was brought up by another user in a Sig owners group, he said "See if you can squeeze the trigger while it's in the holster." So I did. . . and I found that it really isn't that difficult to pull the trigger while it holstered. Yes, my firearm does not have a manual safety but other users sang the praises of this holster so I gave it a try. Simply squeezing my pocket caused the striker to drop. I feel a lighter or similar sized and shaped hard object, a key fob even, could cause an accidental discharge.
Even if my firearm had a manual safety I honestly couldn't recommend this holster just based on how poorly it retains the weapon.
text_fidelity_b: BLACKHAWK 40TP03CT AMBI TecGrip Pocket Holster, Size 03, Coyote Tan

Scuba Choice Diving Stainless Steel Heavy Duty Multi-Purpose Dive Reel 290ft I own a Borzoi puppy and do not have a fenced in yard so I've trained him to run/frolic on 100-200 ft ropes (500 lb paracord from Home Depot). After several months of it getting wrapped around my legs and giving me severe rope burns and scars and spending 15-20 minutes several times a day detangling it to get started, I looked for a reel to use. I tried cheap large plastic extension cord reels and two types of dive reels. This one is the heaviest, best made, with best features. My plan was to remove the dinky rope from this and replace it with the thin paracord but, though the rope fits through the feeder slot, the paracord is such a bigger diameter than what comes with this that less than half the line fit on the real itself so it doesn't work for my use. It's a real shame because nothing else is as easy to use/control. It's possible I could find some really high tensile strength rope that's a smaller diameter but it's probably out of my price range.

The string that came with this lasted a few weeks til it just up and snapped when the rope was stuck on a branch and my puppy took off (at the time it broke he weighed about 45 lbs and now he's over 60 and half grown).

The hand grip is comfortable, hard, but easy to use. The slide lock has 3 settings- stop, go with clicks, and full out go. The clip hardware is fine, I'd probably trust it (strength wise) when my dog is full sized I just don't like the clip type (easy to accidentally unclip so not safe for a dog that's bred to take off and not come back easily).
text_fidelity_b: Scuba Choice Diving Stainless Steel Heavy Duty Multi-Purpose Dive Reel 290ft

Kijaro Dual Lock Folding Chair I'm very pleased with this folding chair. It's far more comfortable than I thought it would be. The mesh and fabric are suspended from the frame, so you never get the hard poke of a metal bar when you're sitting. My back is pretty sensitive to poor seating situations, but I can sit in this for quite some time without any discomfort.

Lots of nicely thought out design features, such as cup holders in each arm, wide fabric on the arms for comfort no matter how you position your arms, and a very easy-to-use folding feature.

The fabric is tough. It's not indestructible, but I expect to be able to get years of use out of it without having to baby it. The frame is also sturdy - no wiggles or wobbles when it fully unfolded. Granted, this type of construction makes the chair heavier than than other folding chairs, but I'm more than happy to deal with a little extra weight in exchange for comfort and solid construction.

My only quibble is that the seat is very wide - about 22 inches at the back and 24 inches at the widest part at the front. A narrower sear width would be nice, and would also allow the chair to take up less room when it's in use. But, better to have it too wide than not wide enough.

Great choice if you're looking for a comfortable folding chair.
text_fidelity_b: Kijaro Dual Lock Folding Chair

text_fidelity_a:
OutdoorMaster Ski Goggles PRO - Frameless, Interchangeable Lens 100% UV400 Protection Snow Goggles for Men & Women Unboxing: Well, to start off, there was no box at all. The Outdoor Master goggles shipped via Amazon in a plastic bag. Inside the bag were the drawstring pouches containing the goggle, and the extra lens that I also ordered. I currently wear a pair of Scott Unlimited II OTG goggles, with the blue pro-lens. It's available for about $80USD, so I think this review of the Outdoor Master Pro (OM Pro) is a fair comparison.

The OM Pro is a spherical lens goggle, and right off the bat I see that the frame (in orange) is more curved than my Scott, also a spherical lens. As well, the OM Pro double layer lens, is thicker than the Scott and less flexible. So when integrated to the magnetic frame the goggle feels heavier and more rigid than the Scott; and doesn't mold to your face as easily. To get around that problem, Outdoor Master uses a thicker layer of foam around the frame (but cheaper closed cell foam). There are 8 small magnets on the lens and frame, changing lenses gives a satisfying click and the connection feels secure. However there have been reviews saying the lens flys off in a real crash, so I reserve judgement until I get a chance to test them in the field.

As for OTG... well yes and no. On my Scott OTG I can comfortable take the on and off over my glasses, the OM Pro has a notch on the frame, but the thick foam gets in the way of my glasses. I have to change to a smaller pair of glasses, or like some have done, cut away the foam to make these truly OTG.

Now for a couple of gripes. First, the OM Pros are larger vertically, perhaps more suited for longer faces. Again, the size coupled with the thick foam presses down on my nose making it hard to breathe freely. You can rotate your helmet back a bit to move the goggles higher on your face, but you end up looking out the bottom half of the lens. So again like some reviews have said, cut away some of the foam. Second, there are NO vents whatsoever on the lens. Partially due to the magnet frame needing to be rigid, there is no place you can drill any holes or cut the lens without damaging the weather seal. This could potentially lead to fogging issues. You only have the top and bottom frame vents to clear moisture.

The lens has minimal distortion and not any more glare than my Scotts. The spare lens pouch is a nice idea, but could they have tried a bit harder to match the curvature of their lens?

For now, 4 stars as a budget minded goggle. I might revise this review once I get some ski days in with this pair of goggles.

**** UPDATE ****
After some on-the-hill testing, this is a pretty good alternative to the name brands in the sub $100 category.

The first day I tried these with the iridium blue lens in sunny conditions. I suddenly felt nauseous .. until I realized like I said earlier, the goggles forced me to look through the bottom half of my bi-focals. So if you wear glasses, this will really depend on your prescription and frame size. The second day I switched to a smaller frame and the goggles let me position it so I looked through the center of my glasses, and all was fine.

I ended up shaving some of the foam to fit better around my nose, and that gave me a more comfortable fit and worked better with my helmet combo. Also, cutting a slot in the foam where my glasses arms were helped with taking them off and on.

On the slope, it was sunny and dry, temps varied from the low teens to near freezing. I did not experience any serious fogging issues, only a little in the gondola with a face mask on. One day it was mixed snow and sun, I was able to swap lenses easily on the hill. I also crashed face first once, and the lens did not pop off. After shaking out some of the snow, it fogged up a bit, but cleared on the rest of the run down and did not fog up again.

Cutters Gamer Padded Receiver Football Gloves, EXTRA GRIP, Youth & Adult sizes I selected these gloves knowing they would be a little small for me but thinking they would fit my teenage son better. As it turns out the size runs small and you really need to buy up one or two sizes to get them to fit just right.

These are athletic gloves and are well-suited for racquet sports, football, basketball, golf and other ball sports as well as biking. They will also work for weight lifting though I would not recommend these for that purpose but instead would recommend something a bit more ruggedized. The palm and print-side fingers are made of a vinyl-like material that is not sticky but slightly tacky and makes gripping and holding very easy. The rest of the gloves are made of light, stretchy material and leatherette material which breathes really well. There is a Velcro wrist strap which tightens the grip around the wrist and keeps the gloves in place.

There are padded sections across the knuckles and on the fingers and thumb which are great for reducing impact damage and pain if you bang your hands (playing racquetball is one situation in which this can happen). This is something I have not seen on work gloves but would appreciate.

These seem to be made very well. I have found no loose threads, uneven seams or imperfections in the materials that would give me any pause with these gloves. I have no issues with the materials and workmanship.

I received a pair of Adult Large gloves. I have hands like a gorilla so I knew they would not fit me very well at all. However, my son is smaller (5’5”, proportional and athletic build) and I figured they would work well for him. I asked him to put them on and try them out, and he complained that they were a bit small even for him, particularly when the Velcro strap was pulled tight. So, for him, an XL is the right size and for me XXL would be right. This is the only issue with these gloves we have found – large should have been appropriate for him, but instead they almost fit.

These are very nice gloves and they are very well made. Just remember to buy a size or two larger than you think you need.

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer Essentially a marriage between Bosu and regular steppers, this device promises to bring the best of both to the home exercise routine. While it does a provide an acceptable basic workout, it does not quite make the mark.

The device itself is large and bulky. You must inflate it with a really lame hand pump. I thought the pump was flimsy. There are no valves, just holes that are plugged after inflation. Once inflated, it is essentially two firm air cushions topped with a balance board. I did find that it held its air, which was good since I do not relish another round with the hand pump. The enclosed dvd comes with instructions and workouts. If you have resistance bands, you are good to go.If not, you need to purchase some because they are not included. The workouts are basic and unlikely to challenge advanced and intermediate exercisers. Overall, this is not a terribly successful hybrid. There is some wobble but probably not enough to make a significant difference in the workout.

As tempting as this concept was, I did not find it superior to or a replacement for either my regular stepper or Bosu. Although the device itself is sturdy, the cost cutting short cuts (hand pump, no valves, no resistance bands) detract. If you are a beginner with a craving for novelty, this device might be a good choice. But overall, I thought it failed to realize its promise.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included) I'm a long-time Fitbit user. I started out with my all-time favorite, the One, which was totally accurate and counted stairs. I replaced it with a Zip, which was also totally accurate but didn't count stairs, and mine went through batteries fast. I owned a couple Altas, that weren't accurate at all and I hated the charging cable.

And that brings me to the Inspire, which I'm pretty happy with. I'm going to start with the things I like about it.

I like the face options and how easy they are to change, the touchscreen - once you get used to it, it's very informative and easy to use, and I like the build quality, which is much nicer than the Zip for the same price I paid for the Zip a few years ago. I guess I got lucky - the unit uses about 10% of the battery per day. I very much prefer the way the Inspire docks in its charging cable - such an improvement over the Alta clips cable! And I've always had good luck getting support from Fitbit - when I had questions about the Inspire, I used their live chat and the rep was helpful and took her time.

Now for a neutral. My Inspire is reasonably accurate but not dead on. If I take 50 steps, it'll count 54 or 47. I can live with that. My One and Zip spoiled me, but both Altas were WAY off, which made me stop using a Fitbit for a while - no sense in wearing one if the counts are off by 25% to 30% (which they were).

There are cons. My first one only applies if you're a long-time Fitbit user and are used to using the wireless dongle so your Fitbit can communite with your computer. You won't be able to use the dongle because the Inspire uses Bluetooth rather than wireless to connect. I liked syncing with my computer, but opted to just sync with my phone as you now have to create a Microsoft account in order to download Fitbit Connect.

I found the band impossible to put on, but I mostly wear it on a clip, and there are some much easier to close and more attractive third-party bands for it on Amazon. It didn't recognize me cycling, and while that didn't bother me, it's worth noting - it would have been cool if that feature had worked.

My Inspire has made me a happy camper. I like wearing a Fitbit, seeing my steps and active minutes - that's why I've owned them. I find the Fitbit dashboard info and the quick stats on the screen motivating, and while I loved my One, the display on the Inspire gives more info more easily thanks to the touchscreen. I like the menus on the Inspire itself, the touchscreen and the charger. Oh, and I think the price ($58 when I bought it) is quite reasonable and a good value. I'm glad I got it :)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves I have owned a pair of Lee Haney lifting gloves with wrist wrap for 19 years and which I used three times per week for about 12 of those years. I still have those gloves and although they are a bit stiff, you'd never know they were used so much as they hardly look worn. Since the Lee Haney gloves are not padded, I decided to try these gloves both because I expected an increase in comfort and as an enticement to get me back into lifting again.

The gloves I received are a size "Large" and they are heavier than any other lifting gloves I've tried before; the pair weighs in at 6.2 ounces according to my dietary food scale. However, you don't notice the weight when wearing them. Below are the pros and cons I noticed during use:

PROS:

1. The gloves are well padded. In fact, the padding is an excellent feature for when I perform lifts where the weight is in the palm of my hand, such as when doing a bench press or incline press or when the weight is evenly distributed throughout the hand such as when doing squats using a [[ASIN:B0000AVAL2 Advanced Fitness Manta Ray]].

2. I usually take a size medium or large in a woman's glove and this size large fit me comfortably.

3. The extra "leather-like" flap that you secure to the fastened wrist wrap offers extra security so that the wrap won't come undone during a lift and the gloves will remain securely fastened.

CONS:

1. The padding on the pinkie finger was uncomfortable for me when doing dead lifts because the bar was evenly distributed through my hand and the padding on the pinkie finger seemed to get in the way. It almost caused a pressure point of discomfort during each entire lift (ascent and descent).

2. The wrist wrap was awkward to fasten because not only did I have to wrap the strap around my wrist, but then I had to flip over the "leather-like" flap and make sure it fastened to the Velcro on the back of the flap.

3. I was bothered by the white tag inside the right glove during lifting. Perhaps the manufacturer could either leave the tags out or put them on the non-Velcro portion of the wrist wrap.

4. I don't like that the two pieces of fabric used to fasten the glove to the cardboard insert it came with remain sewed to the glove. Basically, the gloves arrive with two tags on each glove that fastens to the cardboard packaging. Those tags remain as part of the glove and to me they are annoying as I see no reason to ever use those tags again.

I do think that if men are considering purchasing these gloves, they might want to consider ordering the next size up. My boyfriend always takes a size "Large" in men's gloves and he had to struggle to get these size Large gloves on his hands.

These gloves are thick and although they feel well-made they don't look well-made on close inspection. Therefore, I'm concerned that the stitching on the padding may come loose. When comparing these gloves to my Lee Haney gloves, I doubt they will last as long but only time will tell.

If padding is important, then these gloves offer that and certainly cushion the lifter during many lifts. However, for me I can only give these gloves an average rating because of the cons and my concern that the stitching around the padding will come loose.
text_fidelity_b: Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves

Best Premium Waist Trainer & Trimmer Ab Sweat Belt For Men & Women. (New & Improved) Help Slim your Tummy & Hips Easier Than Ever Before Wearing a Slimming Sauna Belt. 4 Sizes, 2 Colors & Carry Bag. I am definitely one of those skeptics when it comes to products like this. I know that the best way to lose weight is by diet and exercise, And as much as I would love for there to be a magic weight loss product out there, I am very skeptical of anything that sounds too easy.

As far as the construction of the belt, the stitches are secure and even. It looks very well made. The velcro part is basically a large piece of velcro without any additional backing. So when you are handling the velcro, it is a bit on the noisy side. It fits me pretty well, with some extra material to spare. I have no doubts it would fit a smaller waist easily as well as a slightly larger one.I am a size 18. It is surprisingly comfortable. I immediately stood a little taller and straighter. I have tried another waist trainer before and this one is much smoother looking under clothing. When I was wearing my other one, there was extra fabric behind the velcro which caused the velcro fastener to stick out a little more than the rest of the belt. This one gives a smooth line so you can't tell that the fastener is there under your clothing. Although it was pretty comfortable to wear, I found it a little less comfortable when I was sitting down and required some readjusting. It does wonders for lower back pain!

I can't claim to have experienced any weight loss or permanent inches lost, but it does help with posture which helps you to look thinner and it helps with lower back pain, too. And those are nice benefits.

*I did purchase this at a reduced price for the purpose of trying it out and reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.
